mainTopic: When is the שליש holding a גט believed, and what proof is needed that a woman was divorced?
overview: The amud opens with the last line of the משנה, which says three witnesses can make up both required pairs. The גמרא then brings a dispute about a גט held by a שליש: the husband says it was a פקדון, and the שליש says it was for divorce. רב הונא believes the husband, because he would have handed the גט to his wife directly. רב חסדא believes the שליש, because the husband trusted him. רבי אבא challenges רב הונא from a ברייתא that believes a שליש. The גמרא answers that money is different, since it can be forgiven, and defends that answer against two more ברייתות. The גמרא then works through the משנה's need for witnesses, explaining it through רבי אלעזר and a time of persecution. רבה shows when even רב הונא believes the wife, based on a מיגו. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that a גט said to be lost needs two witnesses. The גמרא tests that ruling against the שליש, the husband, and the חזקה that an agent does his job, and the discussion of that חזקה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: one witness can count for both sets
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by saying the two required sets of witnesses can share a witness: one from the first pair, one from the second pair, and a third who joins each of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or one witness from the first pair and one from the second pair, with a third witness joining each of them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It finishes explaining how the two sets of witnesses can be put together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires two separate testimonies, and each one needs two witnesses. This line says you do not need four different people. If one witness from each testimony is different and a third person was present for both events, he completes both pairs, so three witnesses are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The first ones (the first pair of witnesses)
The latter ones (the second pair of witnesses)

phrases.english: or one from the first ones,
phrases.notes: The first pair saw her appoint the agent. The second pair saw him receive the גט and tear it.

phrases.english: and one from the latter ones,
and one joins together with them.
phrases.notes: This third person saw both events, so he counts as the second witness for each pair.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two testimonies can be made up of three witnesses when one witness was present for both events.

steps.title: The dispute: husband says deposit, third party says divorce
steps.stepSummary: The husband claims he gave the גט to the שליש only to hold. The שליש claims it was given for divorce. רב הונא believes the husband, and רב חסדא believes the שליש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: The husband says the גט was given as a deposit, and the third party says it was given for divorce. Who is believed? רב הונא says the husband is believed. רב חסדא says the third party is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a new case and a dispute between two אמוראים about whom to believe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the שליש received the גט. They disagree only about why he got it. If it was a פקדון, the woman is not divorced. If it was for גירושין, the שליש was an agent to deliver it and she is divorced. Each אמורא gives a different answer to who decides that question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
A deposit, something given only for safekeeping
A third party who holds something between two sides

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word שליש does not mean 'one third.' It means the neutral third person holding the גט.

phrases.english: Gemara:
It was stated:
The husband says: as a deposit,
and the third party says: for divorce —
who is believed?
Rav Huna says: the husband is believed,
and Rav Chisda says: the third party is believed.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: the husband is believed. רב חסדא: the שליש is believed.

steps.title: Why רב הונא believes the husband
steps.stepSummary: If the husband really meant to divorce her, he would have given the גט straight to his wife. Handing it to someone else suggests he only wanted it held.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said the husband is believed, because if he had given it to him for divorce, he would have given it to her directly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב הונא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא looks at what the husband did. A man who wants to divorce his wife can just hand her the גט. Since he gave it to a third person instead, the more likely story is that it was only for safekeeping, which backs up the husband's claim.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: the husband is believed —
for if it were so
that he gave it to him for divorce,
he would have given it to her herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: בַּעַל נֶאֱמָן – דְּאִם אִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רב הונא's ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband's choice to give the גט to a third party, and not to his wife, shows it was a פקדון.

steps.title: Why רב חסדא believes the third party
steps.stepSummary: The husband himself chose to trust the שליש by giving him the גט, so the שליש is believed about what it was for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said the third party is believed, since the husband trusted him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב חסדא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not focus on why the husband used a middleman. He focuses on the fact that the husband picked this person and put the גט in his hands. Having trusted him with it, the husband cannot now say the שליש is unreliable about what it was for.

keyTerms.meaning: He trusted him / made him trustworthy

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the husband is believed, because he would have handed the גט to his wife directly. רב חסדא: the שליש is believed, because the husband chose to trust him.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said: the third party is believed —
since he trusted him.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband. By handing over the גט, he showed he trusts this person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: שָׁלִישׁ נֶאֱמָן – דְּהָא הֵימְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reason, for רב חסדא's side of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the husband entrusted the גט to the שליש, the שליש is believed about its purpose.

steps.title: רבי אבא challenges רב הונא from a teaching about a third party
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes a ברייתא: when two sides disagree, the שליש is believed over both of them. That seems to go against רב הונא, who believes the husband over the שליש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא objected: A litigant's own admission is like a hundred witnesses, and a third party is believed over both sides. How so? One side says this and the other side says that, and the third party is believed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא brings a ברייתא to attack רב הונא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes a money dispute where the two sides give different claims, and a שליש holding the money between them is believed over both. If a שליש is believed even against both sides there, it seems he should be believed against the husband here too. That supports רב חסדא and contradicts רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: The admission of a litigant (a person admitting against himself)

steps.confusionAlert: The first line of the ברייתא, about a litigant's admission, is not the point of the attack. The challenge comes from the second part, which says the שליש is believed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba objected:
The admission of a litigant
is like a hundred witnesses,
and a third party is believed more than both of them.
How so?

phrases.aramaic: זֶה אוֹמֵר כָּךְ, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר כָּךְ,
phrases.english: This one says such, and that one says such,
the third party is believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's ruling from steps 2 and 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the husband is believed over the שליש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a שליש is believed even against both sides of a dispute. So he should be believed against the husband too, which contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: Money is different because it can be forgiven
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that believes the שליש is talking about money. Money can be forgiven, so the two sides can agree to accept a third person's word. That does not apply to a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Money is different, because it can be given up as forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by saying רבי אבא's ברייתא is only about money cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may forgive a debt completely, so he may also agree to go by the שליש's word, even if the שליש is wrong. In איסור matters like גיטין, nothing can be forgiven, so the ברייתא proves nothing against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Forgiving or giving up a claim

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the שליש is always believed in money matters because he is more honest. He is believed because the sides are allowed to give up their money rights anyway.

phrases.english: Money is different,
since it was given over to forgiveness.
phrases.notes: He means: an owner is allowed to waive money he is owed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from רבי אבא's ברייתא against רב הונא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to a different kind of case (money, not איסור)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא believes the שליש in every case, including גיטין
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about money, where waiving is possible

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the same rule applies to גיטין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says 'and likewise for גיטין', which seems to show the שליש is believed for a גט too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: and the same is true for גיטין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the money answer by quoting a ברייתא that extends the rule to גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule of believing the שליש also applies to גיטין, then the 'money is different' answer falls apart. רב הונא would be challenged again.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But it was taught:
And the same for גיטין!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer that the rule is limited to money
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer 'שאני ממון' (and with it, רב הונא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא applies the שליש rule to גיטין, which are not money matters

steps.title: 'גיטין' here means money documents
steps.stepSummary: The word גיטין in that ברייתא means money documents, not divorce papers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means money documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'גיטין' in the ברייתא refers to money documents, so it is still a money case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גט can mean any document. If the ברייתא means loan papers and the like, it stays inside the 'money is different' rule. So it does not challenge רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Money documents, such as loan papers

phrases.english: Money documents.
phrases.notes: Read the word גיטין in that ברייתא as money papers, not divorce papers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reading the word differently
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads a word in the source

steps.title: Money documents are called שטרות elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says 'and likewise for שטרות'. That suggests money documents are called שטרות, so גיטין must mean divorce papers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: and the same is true for שטרות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading 'money documents' by pointing to a ברייתא that uses a different word for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If money documents have their own name, שטרות, then the word גיטין should mean something else, namely divorce papers. That brings back the challenge to רב הונא.

phrases.english: But it was taught: and the same for documents!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading 'גיטי ממון'
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of גיטין as money documents
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money documents are called שטרות, so גיטין must mean divorce papers

steps.title: The two ברייתות are separate
steps.stepSummary: The two words do not appear in the same ברייתא, so each ברייתא may simply use its own name for money documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Were they taught next to each other?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the proof only works if both words appeared together in the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one ברייתא listed 'גיטין and שטרות' together, they would have to mean two different things. Since they come from two separate ברייתות, one may call money documents גיטין and the other may call them שטרות. So רב הונא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so? (a word that opens a rhetorical question)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא survives: the ברייתות that believe the שליש can all be read as money cases, where forgiving is possible.

phrases.english: Were they taught next to each other?!
phrases.notes: He means these are two different ברייתות, so each one could use its own word for money papers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שטרות challenge and protects the reading 'גיטי ממון'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the proof does not follow, because the words come from separate sources
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Different words must mean different things
steps.terutzMaskana: Separate ברייתות can use different words for the same thing

steps.title: Why does the משנה need witnesses? Just believe the שליש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה requires two sets of witnesses when a woman's agent receives her גט. The גמרא asks: why not simply believe the person holding the גט?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: a woman who said 'receive my גט for me' needs two sets of witnesses. Two must say 'she said it in front of us', and two must say 'he received it and tore it in front of us'. Why? Let the שליש be believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge from the משנה: if the person holding the גט is trusted, the witnesses should not be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says the שליש is believed because the husband trusted him. If so, the person who received the גט should also be believed about receiving it. Yet the משנה demands witnesses, which seems to show he is not trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: Receive my גט for me (appointing an agent to receive it)
A third party holding the גט

phrases.english: We learned: a woman who said:
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה from step 1, quoted again to build a question.

phrases.english: "Receive my גט for me,"
needs two sets of witnesses:
two who say: "She said it in front of us,"
and two who say: "He received it in front of us, and tore it."
And why?
Let the שליש be believed!
phrases.notes: The שליש here is the person the husband handed the גט to.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן, הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁאָמְרָה: הִתְקַבֵּל לִי גִּיטִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב הונא, the גמרא turns to a challenge from the משנה about trusting the שליש
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the שליש is believed (רב חסדא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the person holding the גט were trusted, the משנה would not need witnesses to prove he received it
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the משנה itself to test whether the person holding the גט is believed, which is the center of the argument between רב הונא and רב חסדא.

steps.title: The torn גט is no longer in the agent's hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in the משנה the גט has already been torn, so the person holding it has nothing left in his hand to be believed about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the גט still coming out from his hand, so that we should believe him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11. A holder is only believed about something he still holds, and in the משנה the גט is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that the holder is believed only works while the item is still in his hands. In the משנה's case the agent already tore the גט, so he has nothing left in his hands. That is why witnesses are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: From under his hand, meaning from his possession

phrases.english: Does the bill of divorce come out
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. The expected answer is 'no', because the גט was already torn.

phrases.english: from his possession, that we should believe him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָא נָפֵיק גִּיטָּא מִתּוּתֵי יְדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 by pointing to a detail of the case: the גט is torn.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the item is no longer in the holder's hands
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The holder of the גט should be believed, so no witnesses should be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A holder is believed only while he still has the item. Here the גט was torn, so witnesses are needed.

steps.title: Why do we need witnesses that the agent received the גט?
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses that the wife appointed the agent make sense. But witnesses that he received the גט seem unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that we need witnesses for 'she said'. But why do we need witnesses for 'he received'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further on the משנה's two sets of witnesses. It accepts one set but questions the need for the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses that the wife said 'receive my גט for me' are needed, because that is not something the agent holds. But at the moment he received the גט, it was in his hands. So by the rule just stated, he should be believed about receiving it without witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (this part is fine)
He received (the agent took the גט)

phrases.english: It works out well for 'she said';
phrases.notes: This means the witnesses who heard the wife say 'receive my גט for me'.

phrases.english: but why do I need witnesses for 'he received'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 12's answer and asks about the second set of witnesses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of witnesses that the agent received the גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the agent received the גט it was in his hands, so he should be believed about that without witnesses.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי אלעזר: witnesses of the handing over make the divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the משנה follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that the witnesses who see the גט being handed over are the ones who make the divorce work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי אלעזר, who says the witnesses of the handing over are what make the divorce work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers step 13 by saying which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, the divorce happens through handing the גט over in front of witnesses. So the receiving needs witnesses, not because the agent is doubted, but because without witnesses there is no divorce at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view the משנה follows here
Witnesses who see the גט being handed over
They cut, meaning they make the divorce take effect

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that witnesses are sometimes needed to make an act happen, not just to prove it.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Whose opinion is this? It is Rabbi Elazar,
who says: Witnesses of the handing over make the divorce take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by saying which opinion the משנה follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Saying which תנא the משנה follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses of receiving are only there to prove something the agent could be believed about.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אלעזר, witnesses to the handing over are what make the divorce happen, so they are needed.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention tearing the גט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs witnesses that the agent tore the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'he tore'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another detail of the משנה: why tear the גט at all? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a woman keeps her גט as proof that she is divorced. So it is strange that the משנה describes the גט being torn.

phrases.english: Why do I need 'he tore'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the receiving to the tearing, another detail of the same משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה describes the גט being torn

steps.title: The משנה was taught in a time of persecution
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the משנה was taught during a time of persecution, which is why the גט was torn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: They taught this in a time of persecution.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the גט was torn: it was a dangerous time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During a persecution, keeping a written גט was dangerous, so it was torn right after it took effect. That explains the tearing, and also why the wife now needs witnesses instead of the document.

keyTerms.meaning: At a time of persecution against Jewish practice

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
They taught this in a time of persecution.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tearing reflects a time of persecution, when keeping a גט was dangerous.

steps.title: רב הונא agrees the wife is believed when she quotes the שליש
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that רב הונא agrees: if the wife says the שליש told her the גט was given to him for divorce, she is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רב הונא agrees that if she says, 'The שליש told me the husband gave it to him for divorce,' she is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רב הונא's view about the שליש. רבה states a case where even רב הונא believes the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא held that the שליש is not believed against the husband. Here רבה adds a limit: when the wife reports what the שליש told her, she is believed. This sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא whose view about the שליש was discussed earlier
A third party who holds a document for both sides

phrases.english: Rabba said: And Rav Huna agrees
that if she says:
The third party told me myself
that he gave it to him for divorce, she is believed.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband, and 'him' is the שליש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the explanation of the משנה and returns to רב הונא's rule about the שליש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רב הונא, the wife is believed when she says the שליש told her the גט was given for divorce.

steps.title: How can the wife be believed when the שליש himself is not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: can it be that the שליש himself is not believed, yet the wife, who only quotes him, is believed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there anything where the שליש himself is not believed, but she is believed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's statement about רב הונא. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife's information comes only from the שליש. If רב הונא does not believe the שליש, it seems strange to believe someone who is just repeating him.

phrases.english: Is there anything
where the third party himself is not believed,
but she is believed?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּשָׁלִישׁ גּוּפֵיהּ לָא מְהֵימַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the statement of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רב הונא believes the wife when she quotes the שליש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone repeating a witness should not be believed more than the witness himself.

steps.title: רבה restates the case: the wife saw it herself
steps.stepSummary: רבה changes his statement. רב הונא agrees the wife is believed when she says she personally saw the husband give the גט to the שליש for divorce. She is believed because of a מיגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if she said: 'In front of me, he gave it to him for divorce,' she is believed. This is because if she wanted, she could have said the husband gave it straight to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem from the last step. The wife is not quoting the שליש. She is telling us what she saw with her own eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the question was: why would the wife be believed when she only repeats the שליש's words, if the שליש himself is not believed? Now the wife is a witness to the handing over herself. She gets credibility from a מיגו: she could have made a stronger claim, that the husband handed the גט directly to her, and she would have been believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (the גמרא is replacing the earlier version)
In front of me, in my presence
'Since': a person is believed because she could have made a stronger claim

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 17. There, the wife was only quoting the שליש. Here, she says she saw the handing over herself, and that is why the מיגו works.

phrases.english: Rather, if she said:
phrases.notes: רבה is taking back the earlier version from step 17 and saying it a new way.

phrases.english: "In front of me, for divorce,
he gave it to him" — she is believed;
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband and 'him' is the שליש.

phrases.english: since if she wanted,
she could have said the husband gave it to her herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by restating רבה's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the case: the wife testifies about what she saw herself, not what the שליש told her.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wife was believed only because she quoted the שליש, which made no sense if he is not believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wife is believed about what she saw herself, based on a מיגו.
steps.whatToRemember: The wife is believed when she says she saw the husband give the גט to the שליש for divorce, because she could have said he gave it to her directly.

steps.title: The lost גט: two witnesses are needed
steps.stepSummary: The husband and the שליש both say the גט was given for divorce. The wife says the שליש gave it to her and it was lost. רבי יוחנן says this is a דבר שבערוה, which needs two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The husband says it was for divorce, the שליש says it was for divorce, and the wife says: 'He gave it to me and it got lost.' רבי יוחנן said: this is a matter of forbidden relations, and such a matter cannot be settled with fewer than two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, related case with a ruling from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the גט was meant for divorce. The only open question is whether it actually reached the wife. Since no גט can be shown, whether she is divorced is a question of forbidden relations. Such a question needs two proper witnesses, and nobody here counts as two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: A third person holding the גט
A matter of forbidden relations (such as whether a woman is married)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next two questions: why not rely on the שליש, or on the husband?

phrases.english: The husband says: "for divorce,"
and the שליש says: "for divorce,"
and she says: "He gave it to me, and it got lost" —
Rabbi Yochanan said:
it is a matter of forbidden relations,
and a matter of forbidden relations needs no fewer than two.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל אֹמֵר לְגֵירוּשִׁין, וְשָׁלִישׁ אוֹמֵר לְגֵירוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new, related case about a גט held by a שליש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the wife claims the שליש gave her the גט and it was lost, she is not considered divorced without two witnesses, because it is a דבר שבערוה.

steps.title: Why not believe the שליש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this case is in doubt. Let us simply believe the שליש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let us believe the שליש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling. It suggests that the שליש's word should be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שליש was the one handling the גט, so maybe he should be trusted, like an agent who testifies about what he did. If so, there would be no need for two witnesses.

phrases.english: But why?
Let us believe the שליש!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that two witnesses are needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שליש's testimony should be enough to settle the question.

steps.title: The גט is no longer in his hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea. The שליש would be believed only if the גט were coming out of his hand now, and it isn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the גט coming out from under his hand, so that we should believe him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing why the שליש is not trusted here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person holding the גט could be trusted because he can hand it over right now. Here the גט is gone, since the wife says it was lost. So the שליש has nothing in his hand to back up his word.

keyTerms.meaning: From under his hand, from his possession

phrases.english: Is the גט coming out
from under his hand, that we should believe him?!
phrases.notes: The wife says the גט got lost, so it is not in the שליש's hand anymore.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָא נָפֵיק גִּיטָּא מִתּוּתֵי יְדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that a needed condition is missing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שליש should be believed because he handled the גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the גט is not coming out of his hand, the שליש is not trusted.

steps.title: Why not believe the husband?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests believing the husband instead. רבי יוחנן himself said a husband who says 'I divorced my wife' is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us believe the husband! For רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a husband who said 'I divorced my wife' is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another way to avoid needing two witnesses: rely on the husband's word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a rule that a husband is believed when he says he divorced his wife. That seems to clash with his own ruling here that two witnesses are needed.

phrases.english: Then let us believe the husband —

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for Rav Chiyya bar Avin said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
a husband who said "I divorced my wife" is believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to step 20, after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that two witnesses are needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself trusts a husband who says he divorced his wife, so the husband's word should settle this case.

steps.title: The husband never said 'I divorced her'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea. The husband did not say 'I divorced her'. He only said he gave the גט to the שליש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he say 'I divorced'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and ends this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule works only when the husband claims the divorce was completed. Here the husband only says he handed the גט to the שליש for divorce. He does not know whether it ever reached his wife, so his words don't prove she is divorced.
steps.whatToRemember: In the lost-גט case, the שליש is not believed because the גט is not in his hand. The husband is not believed because he never claimed he divorced her. So two witnesses are needed.

phrases.english: Does he say "I divorced"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case is different from the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband's word should be enough, based on רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies only when the husband says 'I divorced'. Here he didn't, so two witnesses are needed.

steps.title: Let us presume the agent did his job
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't rely on the חֲזָקָה that an agent carries out his mission. רבי יצחק relies on it even for ערוה: a man whose agent died after being sent to marry an unnamed woman for him is forbidden to every woman in the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us say: there is a presumption that an agent does his job. As רבי יצחק said: if someone tells his agent, 'Go and marry a woman for me' without saying which woman, and the agent dies, the man is forbidden to all the women in the world, because we presume the agent did his job!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. Even if the husband only said he gave the גט to the שליש, we should presume the שליש delivered it, because agents are presumed to do their job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said the husband only testified that he gave the גט to the שליש, not that his wife was divorced. This challenge fills that gap with a חֲזָקָה: the שליש surely finished his mission. The proof from רבי יצחק matters because his case is also about forbidden relations, which answers the concern from step 20 that a דבר שבערוה needs two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal presumption that we may rely on without witnesses
An agent carries out his mission

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the man in רבי יצחק's case is forbidden because he is now married. He is forbidden to all women because any woman could be a close relative of the unknown wife the agent may have married for him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It tests whether a simple presumption can be strong enough even in matters of ערוה, where we are normally very strict.

phrases.english: But let us say: there is a presumption that an agent carries out his mission
phrases.notes: Here the agent is the שליש. The husband gave him the גט, so let's assume he passed it on to the wife.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Yitzchak said:
One who says to his agent:
'Go out and betroth a woman for me' without saying which woman,
and his agent died,
he is forbidden to marry all the women in the world,
phrases.notes: Any woman he marries might be the mother, sister or daughter of the wife the agent picked for him.

phrases.english: because there is a presumption that an agent carries out his mission!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 24 limited the husband's testimony to giving the גט to the שליש, this step tries to close the gap with a presumption that the שליש delivered it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 20 that the case is doubtful and needs two witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without direct testimony that the wife received the גט, the חֲזָקָה that an agent completes his mission should establish delivery. רבי יצחק shows this חֲזָקָה is relied on even in matters of ערוה.
